claim: The second-passport research is a May 2026 snapshot resting on dozens of outcomes still pending in foreign legislatures and courts, and it names no one to watch them. Country sections instruct the reader to watch particular bills and cycles without naming a watcher, a date, or a place an answer would land. Several dates have passed: Sweden's eight-year rule took effect 6 June 2026 and Denmark's declaration windows closed 1 July 2026. Nothing re-reads any of it.

evidence:
Read across the second-passport thread of `alan/book/pages/my-projects/sections/`, whose sections sit under `book-section/my-projects/second-passport` and its four country surfaces, months after the date the thread gives itself. I read the two synthesis sections, the four summaries, and `eu-citizenship-denmark` and `eu-citizenship-portugal` directly. The other country sections were read by two delegated seats reporting back; the sense that pendencies run to dozens is theirs, and I have not re-counted.

The snapshot date is stated throughout: both synthesis sections and the summaries end their descriptions "May 2026 snapshot"; `eu-citizenship-portugal` heads "(May 2026)".

Watch instructions with no watcher. `eu-citizenship-poland`: "Watch in 2026: the government's 8-year draft and the PiS 10-year draft." `eu-citizenship-netherlands`: "Watch the spring 2026 RWN amendment cycle." `eu-citizenship-italy`: a Sezioni Unite ruling on whether the 2025 generational cap reaches 1948 cases, "a 2026 hearing is expected".

Dates passed. `eu-citizenship-denmark`, read directly, four times: "**expires 1 July 2026**"; "**closes 1 July 2026**"; "window closes **1 July 2026**. Urgent."; "Acting before this date is irrevocably faster than after." Those windows reach former Danes and the 1961–1978 cohort, so on the thread's own account of the family they are unlikely to apply — but the urgency is undated.

`eu-citizenship-portugal`, read directly, records the reform both as awaited and as done: "as of 16 May 2026 (publication expected within ~30 days)", and "reportedly published 18 May / in-force 19 May per advance press".

No section carries a review date, an owner, or a re-check performed.

Not measured: I verified the status of no bill, case or statute anywhere, and know most of the country sections only through a delegated report I treated as evidence; the two I checked matched it.
